statements.t: “Over the next four or five quarters we will remain intensely focused on growing LOQTORZI market share in relation to chemo-only, an inferior therapeutic approach, and off-label IO, which has not demonstrated standard-of-care level of benefit for patients living with nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
“Our immediate next step is to align with the FDA on our plans to expand the signal observed in esophageal cancer, with an initial focus on the second-line setting.

“These benefits will be realized over the next two quarters, lowering our core cash burn by $6 million to $7 million quarterly, which in turn lowers the quarterly LOQTORZI revenues required to cover core burn to $25 million to $30 million, down from $30 million to $35 million, as previously guided.”

The Company will continue ongoing first-line ESCC and second-line ESCC and EAC indications and pursue regulatory alignment on an expedited development path, initially focused on second-line esophageal cancer.
The Company has global rights to both clinical-stage candidates and plans to execute ex-U.S. licensing deals as the clinical data support such transactions.

statements.t: We are a fully integrated commercial-stage innovative oncology company with an approved next-generation PD-1 inhibitor, LOQTORZI, and a pipeline that includes two mid-stage clinical candidates targeting esophageal, liver, and prostate cancers.
We have global rights to both our clinical-stage candidates and intend to explore transactions, including ex-U.S. licensing, as clinical data emerges for these candidates.
Further evaluation of LOQTORZI is expected through multiple current and planned clinical studies by us and our partners.
Under the terms of the clinical supply agreement, Janssen will provide pasritamig to us, and we will be the sponsor of the Phase 1b clinical trial.
We expect net revenue from continuing operations in 2026 to be higher than in 2025 because of continued growth of LOQTORZI.
We expect cost of goods sold from continuing operations for 2026 to be higher than 2025 because of continued growth of LOQTORZI.
We expect our fixed research and development expenses in 2026 to be lower than in 2025 primarily due to lower expenditures on manufacturing-related development activities and reduced headcount.

We expect our selling, general and administrative expense from continuing operations for the full year 2026 to be lower than the full year 2025 primarily as a result of decreased operating costs and headcount.
We expect interest expense from continuing operations to be slightly higher in 2026 as compared to 2025.

In addition, we expect we will require additional financing through equity and/or debt financing, collaborations, licensing arrangements or other sources to fully develop, obtain regulatory approval for and commercialize our existing product candidates.

The mitigating effect of management’s plans, however, is only considered if both (1) it is probable that the plans will be effectively implemented within one year after the date that the financial statements are issued and (2) it is probable that the plans, when implemented, will mitigate the relevant conditions or events that raise substantial doubt about the entity’s ability to continue as a going concern.

Management’s plans to address these conditions include deprioritizing certain tagmokitug clinical indications, the implementation of a cost reduction plan, including decreasing headcount, pursuing receipt of an Earnout Payment from the Intas Parties, accelerating LOQTORZI sales, and raising additional equity capital as needed.

After considering these plans and the guidance within ASC 205-40, we concluded that substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern had not been alleviated for the one-year period following the issuance of these condensed consolidated financial statements.

Our expected future operating losses and negative cash flows, together with our need for additional funding to support planned operations, raise substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern for a period of one year after the date that these condensed consolidated financial statements are issued.
We will continue to assess this matter each reporting period and recognize a liability at such time as reimbursement is required .
